**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties** | Property | Value / Description | |----------|---------------------| | **Atomic number** | 1 | | **Symbol** | H | | **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | | **Isotopes** | H‑1 (protium, 99.98 %), H‑2 (deuterium, 0.02 %), H‑3 (tritium, trace) | | **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | | **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | | **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) | | **Electron affinity** | 72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ | | **Atomic radius** | ~53 pm | | **Molecular weight (H₂)** | 2.01588 g mol⁻¹ | | **State at STP** | Colorless, odorless, tasteless diatomic gas | | **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (120.95 K) | | **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | | **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | | **Specific heat capacity (gas)** | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ | | **Heat of formation (H₂(g))** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) | | **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms covalent bonds with most elements; strong reducing agent; reacts with halogens, oxygen, acids, and many metals. | | **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; explosive mixtures with air (4–75 % H₂ in air). | | **Bonding** | Forms H–H single bond; participates in hydrogen bonding (e.g., in water, alcohols). | | **Uses** | • Fuel cell hydrogen (electrochemical conversion to electricity).
• Rocket propellant (liquid or cryogenic).
• Ammonia synthesis (Haber–Bosch process).
• Methanol production.
• Hydride chemistry (NaBH₄, LiAlH₄).
• Metallurgical reducing agent (steelmaking).
• Chemical synthesis (hydrogenation, dehydrogenation).
• Medical imaging (MRI contrast agents).
• Food industry (reduction of fats, decolorization). | | **Safety** | Requires careful handling due to flammability and potential for explosive mixtures; tritium is radioactive. | **General Notes** - Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe, making up ~75 % of its elemental mass. - It exists naturally as a diatomic gas (H₂) under standard conditions but can form various compounds (e.g., H₂O, NH₃, CH₄). - Its unique properties (low density, high specific energy, ability to form hydrogen bonds) make it essential in both natural processes (photosynthesis, respiration) and industrial applications.
